claims.text: Increasing Cr or Al concentration in a high-entropy-alloy coating improves its wear performance.
Increasing Cr or Al promotes rapid formation of a continuous, adherent oxide layer during wear.
A continuous, adherent oxide layer mitigates crack initiation.
A continuous, adherent oxide layer reduces material loss.
The controlled compositional change is a roughly 10–15% relative increase in Cr or Al compared with the baseline formulation.
Moderate sliding loads and temperatures permit active oxidation kinetics without inducing unwanted phase separation.
The proposed structural mediator is a denser and more uniformly distributed Cr2O3- or Al2O3-containing surface layer.
The oxide layer formed during wear is self-healing.
Higher Cr or Al content accelerates formation of the protective oxide film during wear.
Higher Cr or Al content improves maintenance of the protective oxide film during wear.
The protective oxide film diminishes crack nucleation and propagation.
Diminished crack nucleation and propagation reduce the wear rate.
The Cr- or Al-enriched coating should have a lower wear rate than the baseline coating under identical wear conditions.
The Cr- or Al-enriched coating should have a lower friction coefficient than the baseline coating.
Post-wear microscopy should reveal a more continuous and adherent oxide film on the modified coating.
The unmodified baseline forms a less uniform or slower-forming oxide layer under the same wear conditions.
The proposed effect should hold under moderate sliding loads and temperatures when the coating microstructure remains homogeneous.
Extreme temperature, severe loading, or associated phase instability may eliminate the proposed effect.
